about: Illustrations for Le Café des Questions (dialogues 41-60). AI-generated with Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 (Apache-2.0), run on the author's own AWS GPU (one EC2 g7e.2xlarge instance, kit gpu-batch); character designs by the project author. Each episode is an image edit of a cast sheet (the chosen character portraits, painted by the same model on a blank canvas) with the scene prompt. Images marked "published": false had no take that passed QA and are not on the site.

images.prompt: Picture 1 is a reference sheet of the recurring characters, painted on plain paper: first from the left, ROSE, a small 70-year-old woman with fair skin, rosy cheeks and a kind, finely wrinkled face, bright dark eyes, white hair in a neat bun, small reading glasses on a thin chain, a red wool cardigan over a cream blouse and a knee-length charcoal-grey skirt; second from the left, THOMAS, a 45-year-old man with light-tan skin, short dark hair greying at the temples, clean-shaven, a lean face, a navy suit jacket over a light-blue open-collared shirt, no tie; third from the left, HUGO, a tall, slim 22-year-old man with fair skin, short dark-brown curly hair, clean-shaven, a friendly, slightly clumsy smile, a moss-green crew-neck jumper with the sleeves pushed up, dark jeans and a navy-blue apron that is clearly too short for him; on the right, SOCRATE, a grumpy-looking African grey parrot with soft scalloped grey feathers, a pale whitish face patch, pale yellow eyes, a black hooked beak and a bright red tail. Keep each character's face, hair, build, clothes and colours exactly as in Picture 1, but paint a completely new full scene; do not copy the sheet's layout, poses or plain background. Scene: THOMAS, now calm, with no phone, his navy suit jacket open, sits on a bar stool in front of the counter, on the customer side, facing Rose, and has pushed a white cup across the zinc to her. ROSE, standing behind the counter, surprised and delighted, a hand on her chest, turns towards SOCRATE, who has puffed up on his perch by the window with his beak open, whistling. HUGO, behind the counter at its far end, smiles silently while drying a cup. Only one grey parrot exists in this picture, painted once, exactly where described. The setting is a tiny old café in Montmartre, Paris: a short zinc-topped counter with white cups and a sugar bowl, three small round marble tables with bentwood chairs, a worn wooden floor, cream walls, a wooden parrot perch beside a tall window that looks out over grey Paris rooftops with the white dome of the Sacré-Cœur on the left, bare cream plaster walls by the door with only a few small framed watercolours of the blue sea, and behind the counter a row of small postcards whose pictures show only the blue sea. Soft warm autumn afternoon light.
